description: Comms (scripts/comms/comms.gd): who you can call in flight and what they say. Ranges, prices, chances, the clearance rules and the lines. {you} is your ship's name, {them} theirs, {control} the station's traffic control. See docs/runtime/comms.md.

problems: Drive's cooked. Air's fine. Morale isn't.
Out of fuel and out of ideas.
Main engine's dead and so's the backup. We're drifting.
We burned too much on the last leg. Don't ask how.

you_clearance: {control}, this is {you}, inbound. Requesting a berth.
cleared: {you}, {control}. Cleared to berth {berth}. Collar's lit green. Try to hit it.
Copy, {you}. Berth {berth} is yours. Approach slow, we've just had it polished.
{you}, cleared for berth {berth}. Watch the paint.
hold: {you}, hold outside two kilometres. The {other} is coming out of the collar. You'll see them.
Negative on the collar for now, {you}. The {other} is undocking. Hold, and enjoy the view.
after_hold: {you}, the {other} is clear. Cleared to berth {berth}.
Collar's yours, {you}. Berth {berth}. Mind their wake.
already: You're already cleared, {you}. Berth {berth}. We're not saying it twice. That was twice.
fined: {you}, you docked without clearance. That's {fine} and a note on your file. Call in next time.
{you}, nobody cleared you for that collar. {fine}, and your name's on the board in red.
pad_cleared: {you}, pad control. Pad {berth} is yours. Beacon's on. Mind the dust.
Cleared to land on pad {berth}, {you}. Gear down, if you have gear.
camp_cleared: {you}? Yeah. Land on the flat bit. The flatter bit. Not that bit.
Pad's clear, more or less. Come down slow, the foreman's watching.
camp_fined: Next time, call before you drop on my camp. {fine} for the scare.
You land on my camp without a word? {fine}. And a word.
speed: {you}, you're doing {speed} inside two kilometres. Bleed it off or we start writing.
Freighter on approach, you're hot. Slow down. The station doesn't move out of the way.
greet: This is the {them}. What do you need?
{them}. Make it quick, we're on the clock.
patrol: Patrol {them}. Keep it slow near the station and we'll get along fine.
{them}, system patrol. Nothing to report, and we'd like it to stay that way.
fuel_offer: We can spare {t} tonnes at {price} a tonne. Port's cheaper, but the port's over there.
{t} tonnes, {price} a tonne. We'll come alongside. Hold still.
fuel_coming: On our way. Don't do anything clever.
fuel_wait: We can't line up a hose with you moving like that. Hold still.
Stop wriggling, {you}. We're trying to help.
fuel_done: {t} tonnes in. Bill's on its way. Fly safe.
fuel_no: We're doing {speed} the other way. Ask someone who's stopped.
We've barely enough for ourselves. Try a hauler at the port.
tow_offer: We'll take your line. Call it {fee}, and we don't discuss the parking.
We can tow you in for {fee}. It's that or wait for the port tug.
tug_offer: Port tug. {fee} to bring you in, same as always. Sit tight.
Tug here. {fee}, and keep your hands off the throttle.
news_tight: {place} is short of {goods}. Has been for days. You didn't hear it from us.
If you're carrying {goods}, {place} will kiss you. Metaphorically.
news_price: Prices at {place} are {dir} {pct} this week. Make of that what you will.
news_wreck: There's a dead ship out by the station, {km} km off: {wreck}. Nobody's touched it yet.
Saw a wreck on the way in, about {km} km out. {wreck}. Not our business.
news_none: Nothing worth the airtime. Quiet out.
No news. Which is news, round here.
news_again: We told you everything we know. Twice would be making it up.
sos: Mayday, mayday. This is the {them}, {species} registry. {problem} Anyone out there?
Any ship, any ship, this is the {them}. {problem} We've {crew} aboard.
sos_answer: You heard us? Oh, thank everything. Come alongside, we're not going anywhere.
{you}? We see you. Please don't be a salvage crew.
sos_fuel: Fuel? Bless you. {t} tonnes at {price} a tonne, and we owe you a drink.
{t} tonnes. We'll pay {price} a tonne and name a child after you. Small child.
sos_crew: You're taking us off? We'll grab our bags. Somebody grab the cat.
We're coming across. The ship can wait. We can't.
sos_room: You've no room? Then send word to the port. We'll keep the lights on.
sos_bye: We'll make it from here. Thank you, {you}. Really.
Fuelled up and limping home. We owe you.
you_beacon: Beacon's on the {wreck}. Anyone asks, it's taken.
you_split: {them}, this is {you}. Half each, and nobody gets torched?
you_warn: {them}, {you}. That wreck's ours. Find your own.
{them}, back off. Our beacon, our wreck.
rival_there: You're looking at our wreck, {you}. Beacon's on it. Ours.
Salvage tug {them}. That's our beacon on the {wreck}. Move along, or ask nicely.
rival_claim: Salvage tug {them}, coming in on the {wreck}. Our beacon's going on it now.
{them} here. The {wreck}'s ours. Beacon's away. Don't take it personally.
rival_yours: Didn't see your beacon. Didn't look very hard either. Half each, and nobody gets torched?
{them} here. Your beacon, is it? Wreck's big. We'll just take the bits you don't want.
rival_split: Half each it is. We'll take every other piece. Stay off our half.
Deal. Your half, our half. Try to remember which is which.
rival_warned_ok: Fine. Fine! It's yours. We'll find a better one anyway.
Your beacon, your wreck. We're going. Enjoy the rust.
rival_warned_no: Our beacon was on it first, friend. Read the law. We're staying.
Clear off? We were here first. You clear off.
rival_warned_no_yours: Beacon or not, we're cutting. Call the port if you like.
rival_done: We're full. Wreck's all yours, what's left of it.

cleared: Freighter, this is traffic control. Berth {berth} is assigned to you. The collar is lit. Bring her in square.
Acknowledged, freighter. Berth {berth} is yours. The collar has been inspected and signed off. Approach slowly.
Freighter, you are cleared for berth {berth}. The paint was applied with care. Respect it.
hold: Freighter, hold at two kilometres. A vessel is leaving the collar. Safety first, then you.
Negative, freighter. The collar is occupied by a departing ship. Hold position. Patience is a load-bearing virtue.
after_hold: Freighter, the departing ship is clear. Berth {berth} is now assigned to you.
The collar is yours, freighter. Berth {berth}. Watch for their wash.
already: Freighter, you are already cleared. Berth {berth}. A clearance given is a clearance kept.
fined: Freighter, you docked without clearance. {fine}, and it is entered in the record. The record does not forget.
Freighter, an uncleared docking is a breach of care. {fine}. Call in next time.
pad_cleared: Freighter, pad control. Pad {berth} is assigned to you. The beacon is lit. Set her down evenly.
Pad {berth} is yours, freighter. The surface has been checked. Gear down, and gently.
camp_cleared: Freighter. The flat ground east of the hut has been tested. Land there and nowhere else.
The pad is clear. The foreman is watching your descent. He will remember it.
camp_fined: You landed on this camp without a word. {fine}. Our people were under you.
No call, no clearance. {fine} for the danger. We will speak of this.
speed: Freighter, you are fast inside two kilometres. Reduce speed. The station was built to last; do not test it.
Freighter on approach, your speed is unsafe. Slow down. We will not say it twice.
greet: We hear you. State your business.
This is our vessel. Speak, freighter.
We are on a schedule. Be brief, and be clear.
patrol: System patrol. Keep your speed down near the station. We take care of what is ours.
System patrol. All is in order. We intend to keep it so.
fuel_offer: We can spare {t} tonnes at {price} a tonne. The port is cheaper, but the port is far.
We can spare {t} tonnes. The price is on your screen. The port is cheaper, but the port is far.
{t} tonnes, {price} a tonne. We will come alongside. Hold your vessel steady.
{t} tonnes, price on your screen. We will come alongside. Hold your vessel steady.
fuel_coming: Coming alongside. Hold steady. We will do the rest.
We are on our way. Make no sudden moves.
fuel_wait: We cannot couple a hose to a moving ship. Hold still.
Freighter, you are drifting. Hold still. This is for your safety and ours.
fuel_done: Transfer complete. The fuel is in your care now.
The fuel is in. The account is settled. Fly with care.
fuel_no: We are moving fast in the other direction. Ask a ship at rest.
We carry only our own reserve. A reserve is not for sale.
tow_offer: We will take your line. {fee}. Your ship will arrive whole.
We will take your line. The fee is on your screen. Your ship will arrive whole.
We can tow you to port for {fee}. Or you may wait for the tug.
We can tow you to port. The fee is on your screen. Or you may wait for the tug.
tug_offer: Port tug. {fee} to bring you in. Remain still and we will do the work.
Port tug. The usual fee to bring you in. Remain still and we will do the work.
Tug here. {fee}. Keep your hands from the throttle. We have this.
Tug here. The usual fee. Keep your hands from the throttle. We have this.
news_tight: {place} has been short of {goods} for days. A hauler with a conscience would go.
Somebody near here has been short of something for days. A hauler with a conscience would go.
If you carry {goods}, {place} needs you. That is not a figure of speech.
If you carry the right cargo, somebody near here needs you. That is not a figure of speech.
news_price: Prices are moving {dir} this week. Plan accordingly.
We hear {place} is {dir} {pct}. Someone has made a mistake, or a fortune.
We hear prices went {dir}. Someone has made a mistake, or a fortune.
news_wreck: There is a dead ship {km} kilometres out: {wreck}. Its crew deserved better care.
There is a dead ship out by the station. Its crew deserved better care.
We passed a wreck, {km} kilometres out. {wreck}. Nobody has seen to it.
We passed a wreck on the way in. Nobody has seen to it.
news_none: There is no news. That is good news.
Nothing to report. All is holding.
news_again: We have told you all we know. We do not invent.
sos: Mayday, mayday. Kesh vessel in distress. {problem} We require assistance.
Any ship, any ship. {problem} {crew} aboard in our care. Please respond.
sos_answer: You answered. We will not forget it. Come alongside.
We see you, freighter. We are holding. Come as you can.
sos_fuel: Fuel. Thank you. {t} tonnes at {price} a tonne. We will pay in full.
Fuel. Thank you. {t} tonnes. We will pay in full.
{t} tonnes, at {price}. Our household owes yours.
sos_crew: You will take us aboard? We will secure the ship first. Then we come.
We are crossing to you. The ship will be recovered later. We will not.
sos_room: You have no room. Then tell the port. We will keep the lights burning.
sos_bye: We can reach port from here. Our thanks are not small.
Fuelled and under way. This debt is recorded.
rival_there: This wreck is in our care, freighter. Our beacon is on it.
Salvage tug. That beacon is ours. Move on, or ask with respect.
rival_claim: Salvage tug, approaching the wreck. We are placing our beacon now.
This wreck is now in our care. The beacon is set. Do not interfere.
rival_yours: We did not see your beacon. We should have. Half each, and no one is hurt?
Your beacon, then. The wreck is large. We will take only what you leave.
rival_split: Half each. We will take every other piece. Respect our half.
Agreed. Your half, our half. The agreement is binding.
rival_warned_ok: Your beacon was first. The wreck is yours. We withdraw.
The claim is yours by right. We go.
rival_warned_no: Our beacon was placed first. The law is with us. We remain.
We were here first. You will leave, not us.
rival_warned_no_yours: Beacon or not, we are cutting. Call the port.
We have heard you. We continue.
rival_done: We are finished. What remains is yours.
Our hold is full. The wreck is yours to care for.

cleared: Freighter. Berth {berth}. Collar lit. Two metres a second, no more.
Copy, freighter. Berth {berth}. Square approach. Polished yesterday.
Cleared, berth {berth}. Mind the paint. Paint is mass we did not want to add twice.
hold: Freighter. Hold at two kilometres. Departure in the collar. Ninety seconds.
Negative. Collar occupied. Hold. Do not burn fuel waiting.
after_hold: Freighter. Berth {berth}. Their wake decays in thirty seconds. Wait for it.
already: Already cleared. Berth {berth}. Repeating costs air.
fined: No clearance. {fine}. Next time, one call. It weighs nothing.
pad_cleared: Pad control. Pad {berth}. Beacon on. Dust settles in four seconds here.
Pad {berth}. Gear down. Light touch. Low gravity forgives, mostly.
camp_cleared: Flat ground, forty metres north of the hut. Exactly there.
Pad clear. Descend slowly. The foreman measures.
camp_fined: No call. {fine}. The dust took an hour to settle.
speed: Freighter, you are fast inside two kilometres. Bleed it. Now.
Too fast on approach. Slow down. The station's mass exceeds yours.
greet: Proceed. We are on a burn window.
patrol: System patrol. Speed limits near the station. Observe them.
System patrol. Nominal. Keep it nominal.
fuel_offer: {t} tonnes spare. {price} a tonne. Port is cheaper per tonne, not per hour.
{t} tonnes spare. Price on your screen. Port is cheaper per tonne, not per hour.
{t} tonnes, price on your screen. Coming alongside. Hold attitude.
fuel_wait: You are moving. Hose alignment fails. Hold.
Stop drifting. We measure in centimetres.
fuel_no: Wrong vector. Ask a ship at rest.
No margin. We carried exactly enough.
tow_offer: Line accepted. Fee on your screen. Parking excluded.
Tow to port, {fee}. Alternative: port tug, later.
Tow to port, fee on your screen. Alternative: port tug, later.
tug_offer: Port tug. Standard fee. Hold still.
Tug. Standard fee. Hands off the throttle.
news_tight: Somebody near here: short of something. Several days.
Somebody near here needs your cargo. Demand exceeds supply. Considerably.
news_wreck: Debris field, {km} kilometres out. {wreck}. Mass going to waste.
Wreck on the way in. Mass going to waste.
sos: Mayday, mayday. Ilyan vessel. {problem} Requesting assistance.
Any ship. {problem} {crew} aboard. Air for six days.
sos_answer: Acknowledged. Grateful. Match velocity when able.
We see you. Relief exceeds expectation.
sos_fuel: {t} tonnes. {price}. A fair exchange, for once.
{t} tonnes. A fair exchange, for once.
sos_crew: Transferring. Personal mass under ten kilograms each. We are fast.
Crossing now. The ship stays. We don't.
sos_room: No room. Notify the port. We will conserve power.
sos_bye: Sufficient to reach port. Thank you.
rival_there: Our wreck. Our beacon. Move on.
Salvage tug. Beacon placed. Claim valid.
rival_claim: Wreck claimed. Beacon away. Nothing personal.
rival_yours: Your beacon. Missed it. Split? Fifty-fifty. Fair.
Your claim. Large wreck. We take the remainder.
rival_split: Fifty-fifty. Alternating pieces. Stay on yours.
rival_warned_no: Our beacon was first. Check the timestamp. Staying.

cleared: Freighter, welcome in. Berth {berth} is ready for you. The collar's lit. Drift in easy.
Copy, friend. Berth {berth} is yours. Come in gently, like the tide.
Cleared for berth {berth}, freighter. Mind the paint. Someone took a long time over it.
hold: Freighter, ease off at two kilometres. Someone's leaving the collar. Let them go first.
Not yet, friend. The collar's busy with someone going home. Hold, and breathe.
after_hold: They're clear, freighter. Berth {berth}'s yours now. Come in.
The collar's yours, friend. Berth {berth}. Their wake will settle. Give it a moment.
already: You're already cleared, friend. Berth {berth}. It's waiting for you.
fined: Freighter, you docked without a word. {fine}. Everyone in the collar felt that.
No clearance, friend. {fine}. It isn't the money. It's everyone else.
pad_cleared: Freighter, pad control. Pad {berth} is yours. Beacon's on. The dust goes everywhere. Go gently.
Pad {berth} is ready for you. Gear down, and soft. The ground remembers.
camp_cleared: Freighter? Welcome. The flat ground past the water tanks. Not near the tanks.
The pad's clear. Come down slow. The foreman's growing beans out there.
camp_fined: You came down without calling. {fine}. You shook the whole camp.
No word before you landed? {fine}. Everyone here felt it.
speed: Freighter, you're coming in fast inside two kilometres. Ease off, for all of us.
Freighter on approach, slow down, please. Everything you do here, everyone feels.
greet: We hear you, friend. Go ahead.
This is us. What do you need?
Go ahead. We're listening, all of us.
patrol: System patrol. Keep it gentle near the station, and we'll all get along.
System patrol. Calm waters today. Let's keep them that way.
fuel_offer: We can share {t} tonnes, at {price} a tonne. The port's cheaper, but the port's a long swim.
We can share {t} tonnes. The price is on your screen. The port's cheaper, but the port's a long swim.
{t} tonnes, {price} a tonne. We'll drift alongside. Stay still for us.
{t} tonnes, price on your screen. We'll drift alongside. Stay still for us.
fuel_coming: Drifting alongside now. Stay still for us.
On our way, friend. Nothing sudden.
fuel_wait: You're drifting, friend. We can't line up the hose. Hold still.
fuel_done: The fuel's in. The bill follows. Safe currents.
fuel_no: We're flowing the other way, friend. Ask someone at rest.
We've only enough for ourselves. Try a hauler at the port.
tow_offer: We'll take your line, friend. {fee}. Nobody gets left out here.
We'll take your line, friend. The fee's on your screen. Nobody gets left out here.
We can bring you in for {fee}. Or wait for the tug. Your choice.
We can bring you in. The fee's on your screen. Or wait for the tug. Your choice.
tug_offer: Port tug. {fee}, same as always. We've got you.
Port tug. The usual fee. We've got you.
Tug here. {fee}. Let go of the throttle, friend.
Tug here. The usual fee. Let go of the throttle, friend.
news_tight: {place} has been short of {goods} for days. They're struggling.
Somebody near here has been short of something for days. They're struggling.
If you've got {goods}, {place} needs it more than you do.
If you've got the right cargo, somebody near here needs it more than you do.
news_price: Prices at {place} are {dir} {pct}. Someone's having a hard week.
Prices went {dir} this week. Someone's having a hard week.
Heard {place} is {dir} {pct}. It always comes back round.
Heard prices went {dir}. It always comes back round.
news_wreck: There's a dead ship {km} kilometres out. {wreck}. Somebody should see to it.
There's a dead ship out by the station. Somebody should see to it.
We passed a wreck, {km} kilometres out. {wreck}. Sad, drifting thing.
We passed a wreck on the way in. Sad, drifting thing.
news_none: Nothing worth the airtime. Quiet, everywhere.
news_again: We've told you all we know, friend.
sos: Mayday, mayday. Vey ship in trouble. {problem} Is anyone out there?
Any ship, any ship. {problem} {crew} of us aboard. Please.
sos_answer: You heard us. Oh, thank you. Come alongside, we're not going anywhere.
We see you, friend. We're so glad we see you.
sos_fuel: Fuel. Thank you. {t} tonnes at {price}, and you'll eat with us one day.
Fuel. Thank you. {t} tonnes, and you'll eat with us one day.
{t} tonnes. {price} a tonne. We'll remember this.
sos_crew: You'll take us? We're coming. Someone bring the plants.
We're crossing over. The ship can wait. We can't.
sos_room: No room? Then tell the port about us. We'll keep the lights on.
sos_bye: We'll make it from here. Thank you. Really.
Fuelled and flowing home. We owe you.
rival_there: That wreck's ours, friend. Our beacon's on it.
Salvage tug here. That's our beacon. Move along, or ask nicely.
rival_claim: Salvage tug, coming in on the wreck. Our beacon's going on it.
That wreck's ours now. Beacon's away. Nothing personal.
rival_yours: Didn't see your beacon, friend. Half each, and nobody gets hurt?
Your beacon, is it? Plenty here for everyone. We'll take what you leave.
rival_split: Half each. We'll take every other piece. Leave ours be.
Deal. Your half, our half. Share and share alike.
rival_warned_ok: Your beacon was first. It's yours. We'll go.
Fair enough. We're going. Look after it.
rival_warned_no: Our beacon was first, friend. We're staying.
We were here first. We'd rather you went.
rival_warned_no_yours: Beacon or not, we're cutting. Call the port if you have to.
We hear you. We're still cutting.
rival_done: We're done. The rest is yours.
Our hold's full. Everything left is yours.

cleared: Freighter, we see you. We are giving you berth {berth}. The collar is lit. We are all watching.
Copy, freighter. Berth {berth} is ours and now yours. Come in slow. We just polished it together.
Cleared for berth {berth}, freighter. We painted that collar. All of us.
hold: Freighter, hold at two kilometres. One of us is coming out of the collar. You will see them.
Not yet, freighter. We are moving a ship out. Hold, and we will call you.
after_hold: Freighter, they are out. We are giving you berth {berth}.
The collar is yours, freighter. Berth {berth}. We will all mind their wake.
already: We already cleared you, freighter. Berth {berth}. We all heard us say it.
fined: Freighter, you docked without calling. {fine}. We all saw.
Nobody cleared you. {fine}. And we will talk about it at supper.
pad_cleared: Freighter, this is us at pad control. Pad {berth} is yours. Beacon on. We are watching the dust.
Pad {berth} for you, freighter. Gear down. We will come and look at your legs after.
camp_cleared: Freighter? Yes. We are all at the hut. Land on the flat bit. We will wave.
The pad is clear. Come down slow. Everyone is watching. Everyone always is.
camp_fined: You landed on us without calling. {fine}. We were having lunch.
No word? {fine}. We will all remember.
speed: Freighter, we see you fast inside two kilometres. Slow down. We are all inside this station.
Freighter on approach, you are hot. Slow down. We live here.
greet: This is us. All of us. What do you need?
Go ahead, freighter. We are all listening.
patrol: System patrol. We keep it slow near the station. You will too.
System patrol. Nothing to report. We like it that way.
fuel_offer: We can spare {t} tonnes at {price} a tonne. The port is cheaper, but we are closer.
We can spare {t} tonnes. The price is on your screen. The port is cheaper, but we are closer.
{t} tonnes, {price}. We will come alongside. Hold still. We are good at close.
{t} tonnes, price on your screen. We will come alongside. Hold still. We are good at close.
fuel_coming: We are coming alongside. Close. Hold still.
On our way. All of us. Do not do anything clever.
fuel_wait: We cannot line up the hose with you moving. Hold still.
Stop wriggling, freighter. We are trying to help, together.
fuel_done: That is your fuel. Our tanks thank your account.
Fuel in. Bill sent. We will think of you warmly.
fuel_no: We are all going the other way. Ask a ship that has stopped.
We have just enough for us. And there are many of us.
tow_offer: We will take your line. {fee}. We do not discuss the parking.
We will take your line. The fee is on your screen. We do not discuss the parking.
We can tow you in for {fee}. Or wait for the tug. We would wait with you.
We can tow you in. The fee is on your screen. Or wait for the tug. We would wait with you.
tug_offer: Port tug. {fee}, same as always. Sit tight. We have you.
Port tug. The usual fee. Sit tight. We have you.
Tug here. {fee}. Hands off the throttle. We are holding it.
Tug here. The usual fee. Hands off the throttle. We are holding it.
news_tight: {place} is short of {goods}. We heard it from everyone.
Somebody near here is short of something. We heard it from everyone.
If you carry {goods}, take it to {place}. They need it. We would.
If you carry the right cargo, somebody near here needs it. We would take it.
news_price: Prices at {place} are {dir} {pct}. Everyone is talking about it.
Prices went {dir} this week. Everyone is talking about it.
We heard {place} is {dir} {pct}. We hear everything.
We heard prices went {dir}. We hear everything.
news_wreck: There is a dead ship {km} kilometres out: {wreck}. Nobody has gone in. We would.
There is a dead ship out by the station. Nobody has gone in. We would.
We passed a wreck, {km} kilometres out. {wreck}. Somebody should fix it, or take it.
We passed a wreck on the way in. Somebody should fix it, or take it.
news_none: No news. We are as surprised as you.
Nothing. Quiet out here. Too quiet for us.
news_again: We told you everything we know. Twice would be gossip.
sos: Mayday, mayday. Orun ship, all of us aboard. {problem} Anyone?
Any ship, any ship. {problem} {crew} of us here. Together, but stuck.
sos_answer: You heard us! We all heard you hear us. Come alongside.
We see you. All of us see you. Please do not be a salvage crew.
sos_fuel: Fuel! {t} tonnes at {price}. We will all owe you supper.
Fuel! {t} tonnes. We will all owe you supper.
{t} tonnes, {price} a tonne. We will name a tunnel after you.
{t} tonnes. We will name a tunnel after you.
sos_crew: You will take us? We are packing. Together. This could take a while.
We are coming across. All of us. The ship can wait.
sos_room: No room? Then tell the port. We will keep the lights on and each other company.
sos_bye: We will make it from here. Thank you, from all of us.
Fuelled and limping home together. We owe you.
rival_there: That is our wreck, freighter. Our beacon. We all agreed.
Salvage tug. That beacon is ours. Move along, or come and ask us nicely.
rival_claim: Salvage tug, coming in on the wreck. We are putting our beacon on it.
That wreck is ours now. Beacon away. Nothing personal. We like you.
rival_yours: We did not see your beacon. We did not look. Half each, and we all go home?
Your beacon? The wreck is big. We will take the bits you do not want. We share.
rival_split: Half each. We take every other piece. Stay off our half.
Deal. Your half, our half. We will all remember which is which.
rival_warned_ok: Fine. Fine! It is yours. We will find another. Together.
Your beacon, your wreck. We are going. Enjoy it.
rival_warned_no: Our beacon was first. We all saw it. We are staying.
Clear off? We were here first. All of us.
rival_warned_no_yours: Beacon or not, we are cutting. Call the port. We will wait.
We heard you. All of us. We are still cutting.
rival_done: We are done. Pleasure, mostly. Mostly for us.
We are full. What is left is yours. We left you good bits.

species_sound.description: How each species sounds on top of its recorded voice (VoiceBank.species_bus): 'lead_s' seconds of its own language before the translator catches up (the first call from a caller each flight; 'lead_again_s' after), 'layers' extra copies of the voice pitched by 'pitch' at 'db', and effects on the voice itself. Humans need no translator.
